\section{What the analysis notices}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em]
  \item \finding{warning} \texttt{halo\_exchange/?} reports 0 messages but the fabric logged 14: the collective's own accounting disagrees with the traffic it produced.
  \item \finding{warning} Ranks 8, 14 appear in the log without participating; the declared world size is 8. Shared worker pools let a worker register against the wrong job, which inflates the apparent rank count.
  \item \finding{warning} The cost model's $\alpha$ and $\beta$ here are a median fallback, not a fit: the regression returned a negative slope ($\beta=-0.0015$\,s/token) and was rejected. That happens when queueing dominates latency, because the wait enters the measured time but not the token count, so the relationship the fit looks for is not in the data. Any latency prediction from this run's calibration is a median, not a model.
  \item \finding{ok} 24 rank reattachment(s) occurred, up to incarnation 4: agent processes were replaced mid-run while the rank roles, their mailboxes, and their context accounts persisted.
  \item \finding{ok} All 3 checkable collective(s) sent exactly the number of messages their closed-form cost expression predicts.
\end{itemize}
